title: The Alternate Thomassé conjecture on sibling numbers of relations
statement:
Let $R=(V,E)$ be a relation of arbitrary cardinality, where $V$ is a non-empty domain and $E$ is an $n$-ary relation on $V$ for some positive integer $n$. The **sibling number** $Sib(R)$ is the number of isomorphism classes of relations equimorphic to $R$, where two relations are equimorphic when each embeds in the other.

**The Alternate Thomassé conjecture.** For every relation $R$ of arbitrary cardinality,

$$
Sib(R)=1\quad\text{or}\quad\infty.
$$

This is the unrestricted-cardinality alternative to Thomassé's conjecture and is the version addressed for countable $NE$-free posets in the paper. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved in general.
source_name: Davoud Abdi, “A Proof of the Alternate Thomassé Conjecture for Countable NE-Free Posets”, arXiv:2209.03893 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03893

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2022).
